setlist.title: Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deal** (1 review): Features loud, sharp guitar solos that sound like holding a downed power line in his teeth [4]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Garcia plays loud, sharp solos, described as holding a downed power line in his teeth [4]
- **I Second That Emotion** (1 review): The reviewer identifies this as their favorite cover song the Grateful Dead ever performed [8]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): The extended jam into Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad is described as hair-standing [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **I Second That Emotion**: rare: 7 archived performances [14]
- **The Pump Song**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd71-04-15.sbd.eD.11652.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 100 min; rated 4.58/5 by 24 [1]

## Around the show

- Attendees threw a shopping bag full of oranges into the small, old gym crowd [6]
- The band maintained a running conversation with the primed, gliding crowd in the intimate setting [6]
- New Riders of The Purple Sage opened with Jerry Garcia playing pedal steel [12]
- Mickey Hart had left the band, leaving the Grateful Dead as a five-piece group [12]
- A fan named Allen repeatedly threw oranges at the reviewer during the performance [12]
- The reviewer sat ten feet from Jerry and lost feeling in their left foot for five years [13]
- The performance style develops into the later April 1971 Fillmore shows, specifically the 4-25-29 dates [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-04-15.sbd.eD.11652.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill O.; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The recording is a DAE transfer with high, secure, offset corrected settings [1]
